newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Electricidad expects slim '96 profit.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Electricidad expects slim '96 profit.

text.p: Venezuela's Electricidad de Caracas, the bellwether stock of the Caracas Stock Exchange, expects to post only a small profit this year in spite of recent increase in rates, a top company executive said on Monday.
"We expect to register profits in the second half and to end the year with a meagre profit given the size of the company," said the official, who requested anonymity.
Electricidad de Caracas reported last week 9-month net inflation-adjusted profits of 42 billion bolivars, down from 57 billion in the first three quarters of 1995.
The official said the company's investment plans "remain frozen for the time being" and that only those previously approved were being carried out.
He said he hoped the situation would improve from January "when the government says there will be another increase in rates."

The government authorized a hike in electricity rates a month ago, for the third time this year. Electricidad de Caracas said at the time the rise translated into a 10.4 percent increase in rates, falling short a of hoped-for 13 percent rise.
